changelog: `apm marketplace add OWNER/REPO#ref` and `HOST/OWNER/REPO#ref` register the named ref instead of tracking `main` (#4217)

ledger_row.summary: apm marketplace add OWNER/REPO#ref kept the #ref inside the stored repository URL, tracked main, failed the fetch, and printed an unpinned warning suggesting OWNER/REPO#ref#v1.0.0.

red: APM_E2E_TESTS=1 APM_BINARY_PATH="$(uv run which apm)" uv run --extra dev pytest tests/integration/test_marketplace_registered_ref_lifecycle.py::test_shorthand_fragment_ref_registers_the_named_ref -n 0 -p no:cacheprovider -q -> FAILED [owner-repo] and [host-owner-repo]: `assert result.returncode == 0` (exit 1; '[!] Pin this git marketplace with a #ref (for example, team/platform/agent-catalog#release/pilot#v1.0.0)' then '[x] Failed to fetch marketplace')
green: APM_E2E_TESTS=1 APM_BINARY_PATH="$(uv run which apm)" uv run --extra dev pytest tests/integration/test_marketplace_registered_ref_lifecycle.py::test_shorthand_fragment_ref_registers_the_named_ref -n 0 -p no:cacheprovider -q -> 2 passed (module: 4 passed)
owner: src/apm_cli/marketplace/registration.py (split_source_fragment_ref, used by parse_registration_source for both apm marketplace add and the user-manifest marketplaces: reconcile); helper is_shorthand_marketplace_source in src/apm_cli/marketplace/source_identity.py
notes: Chose HONOR over refuse: the CLI's own unpinned-source warning already prints '<OWNER/REPO>#v1.0.0' as the fix, so the hint must be runnable; the test executes that printed hint and asserts the registry ref is v1.0.0. A '#' stays part of local paths and SCP/SSH forms keep their existing fragment refusal. Docs: reference/cli/marketplace.md accepted forms and apm-guide commands.md updated. The user-manifest marketplaces: source field inherits the same grammar through parse_registration_source.
